blocks.task_summary: Show that the three planes do not intersect by eliminating a variable to obtain contradictory parallel equations.
method_path: Eliminate one variable from two pairs of plane equations
Obtain two equations in two variables with identical left-hand side but different right-hand side
Conclude the system is inconsistent, hence the three planes do not intersect
accepted_alternatives: Method 2: Compute vector product of normals n1 x n2 = (-1,-5,-3), form line r = (1,-2,0) + lambda(1,5,3), substitute into Pi3 to obtain -15 = 32 (contradiction)
Method 3: Eliminate variable y to obtain -3y+5z = 6 and -3y+5z = 100, giving 0 = 94 (contradiction)
Any valid elimination leading to contradictory equations

evidence.basis: Method 1: M1 attempt to eliminate a variable; A1 first equation in two variables; A1 second equation; R1 lines are parallel, contradiction, hence planes do not intersect AG
Method 2: A1 vector product of normals = (-1,-5,-3); A1 r = (1,-2,0) + lambda(1,5,3); M1 substitute into Pi3; R1 -15=32 contradiction, hence planes do not intersect AG
Method 3: M1 eliminate variable; A1 -3y+5z=6; A1 -3y+5z=100; R1 0=94 contradiction, hence planes do not intersect AG

blocks.task_summary: Verify P(1,-2,0) lies on Pi1 and Pi2; find a vector equation of L, the line of intersection of Pi1 and Pi2.
method_path: Substitute P(1,-2,0) into Pi1: 2(1)-(-2)+0 = 4 and Pi2: 1-2(-2)+3(0) = 5 to verify
accepted_alternatives: Method 2: Eliminate a variable from Pi1 and Pi2 to obtain parametric equations, e.g. x = t, 5x - y = 7 so y = 5t - 7, 3x - z = 3 so z = 3t - 3, giving r = (0,-7,-3) + lambda(1,5,3) or equivalent

evidence.basis: Part (i): A1 for Pi1: 2+2+0=4 and Pi2: 1+4+0=5. Part (ii) Method 1: M1 vector product of normals; A1 direction (-1,-5,-3); A1A1 r = (1,-2,0) + lambda(-1,-5,-3). Note: Award A1A0 if r= is missing.
Method 2: M1 eliminate variable; A1 obtain parametric form; A1A1 r = (0,-7,3) + lambda(1,5,-3) or equivalent. Note: Award A1A0 if r= is missing.

blocks.task_summary: Find the distance between line L and plane Pi3.
method_path: Form line L1 through P(1,-2,0) with direction normal to Pi3: n3 = (-9,3,-2)
accepted_alternatives: Method 2: Use unit normal form. Plane Pi3: (-9x+3y-2z)/sqrt(94) = 32/sqrt(94). Parallel plane Pi4 through P: (-9x+3y-2z)/sqrt(94) = -15/sqrt(94). Distance = |32-(-15)|/sqrt(94) = 47/sqrt(94) = sqrt(94)/2

evidence.basis: Method 1: (M1) form L1 with direction n3; A1 L1 equation; M1 substitute into Pi3; A1 t = 1/2; (M1) attempt distance from P to point on Pi3; A1 distance = sqrt(94)/2
Method 2: (M1) unit normal equation of Pi3; A1 = 32/sqrt(94); M1 plane Pi4 through P parallel to Pi3; A1 unit normal = -15/sqrt(94); (M1) distance between planes; A1 = 47/sqrt(94) = sqrt(94)/2
